The heavens opened to Ezekiel by a river in exile. How does God meet people far from home?
Ezekiel saw living creatures and wheels full of eyes. What does this vision show about God's power and presence?
Ezekiel saw "the likeness of the glory of the Lord" and fell on his face. How do you respond to God's glory?
The Spirit set Ezekiel on his feet. How does God's Spirit strengthen you?
God sent Ezekiel to speak "whether they hear or refuse to hear." How do you stay faithful when people don't listen?
God told Ezekiel to eat the scroll. How do you take God's word inside you?
The scroll tasted as sweet as honey. When has God's word been sweet to you?
God made Ezekiel a watchman to warn the people. Who might you need to gently warn?
God's glory met Ezekiel in the valley. How does God meet you in low places?
Ezekiel acted out the siege of Jerusalem. What does this show about how seriously God takes sin?
Ezekiel ate rationed bread as a sign of scarcity. What does this teach about what sin costs a people?
Jerusalem had rejected God's rules more than the nations. What does privilege bring with it?
God says his eye will not spare, yet he acts so they will know he is the Lord. What does God want people to know about him?
"You shall know that I am the Lord." How has God made himself known to you, even through hard times?
A remnant would remember God and loathe their evil. What does true repentance look like?
"The end has come." What does this teach about God's patience coming to an end?
"Their silver and gold are not able to deliver them in the day of the wrath of the Lord." What do people trust in for security?
Ezekiel saw idols hidden inside the temple. What hidden idols might be in our hearts?
The elders said, "The Lord does not see us." Why do we act as if God doesn't see?
God marked those who sighed and groaned over the abominations. What does it mean to grieve over sin?
Ezekiel cried out for mercy for the people. How can you pray for mercy for others?
The house was filled with the cloud and the brightness of the glory of the Lord. What does God's glory mean?
The glory of the Lord departed from the threshold of the temple. What would it mean to lose God's presence?
God says, "I have been a sanctuary to them for a while in the countries where they have gone." How is God your sanctuary?
"I will remove the heart of stone from their flesh and give them a heart of flesh." What heart change do you need?
Ezekiel acted out going into exile. How does God use visible signs to teach?
God says, "None of my words will be delayed any longer." How does this show God's faithfulness?
False prophets follow their own spirit and have seen nothing. How can you discern true from false teaching?
They whitewashed a flimsy wall, saying "Peace" when there was no peace. Why is false comfort dangerous?
The elders had taken their idols into their hearts. What idols might be in your heart?
"Repent and turn away from your idols." What do you need to turn from?
A vine that bears no fruit is useless for anything. What fruit does God want from your life?
Jerusalem was like a vine fit only for burning because of unfaithfulness. What does faithfulness to God look like for you?
God found Jerusalem as an abandoned baby and cared for her. How has God cared for you when you were helpless?
Israel trusted in her beauty and turned away. How can God's gifts become reasons to forget him?
God says, "I will remember my covenant... and establish for you an everlasting covenant." What does God's faithfulness mean to you?
The king broke his covenant oath. Why does God care so much about keeping our word?
God will plant a tender twig that becomes a noble cedar. How does this point to Jesus' kingdom?
God says each person is responsible before him. What does this mean for you?
"Have I any pleasure in the death of the wicked... and not rather that he should turn from his way and live?" What does this show about God's heart?
"Make yourselves a new heart and a new spirit! Why will you die?... Turn, and live." Where do you need to turn and live?
Ezekiel lamented over Israel's princes. What does lament teach you about grief and failure?
The vine once fruitful was uprooted. What does this show about pride and loss?
God acted for the sake of his name so it would not be profaned. Why does God care about his name?
God promised to bring his people out and purge rebels. What does God's refining do?
God says, "You shall know that I am the Lord, when I deal with you for my name's sake, not according to your evil ways." What does God's grace show?
Ezekiel was told to groan with a breaking heart. How should we feel about coming judgement?
God will overturn things until "he comes, the one to whom judgement belongs." How does this point to Jesus?
God lists sins of injustice against parents, strangers and the poor. Which of these does our culture overlook?
God looked for someone to stand in the breach but found none. How can you stand in the gap for others in prayer?
Two sisters turned to other lovers. What draws our hearts away from God?
"Because you have forgotten me and cast me behind your back..." How do we cast God behind our backs?
The cooking pot pictured a city whose filth would not come clean. What do you need God to cleanse?
Ezekiel's wife died and he obeyed God in his grief. How can faith hold in loss?
God judged Ammon for rejoicing over Israel's ruin. Why is it wrong to rejoice when others fall?
God judged those who took revenge with malice. Why does God forbid revenge?
God judged Tyre for gloating. What does God say about pride in others' downfall?
The coastlands trembled at Tyre's fall. What does this show about how quickly earthly glory can end?
Tyre was famous for its wealth and trade, but it sank. What does this show about trusting in riches?
The sailors wailed when the great ship sank. What does this teach about putting hope in wealth?
The prince of Tyre said, "I am a god." How does wealth tempt us to pride?
God promised his people would dwell securely and know he is the Lord. What security does God give?
Pharaoh said, "My Nile is my own; I made it for myself." How do we claim credit for what God gives?
Egypt had been a staff of reed to Israel that broke when leaned on. What do people lean on that cannot hold them?
Egypt's helpers would fall. What does this show about relying on human strength?
God strengthened Babylon and broke Pharaoh's arms. What does this show about God ruling over nations?
The great cedar was brought low because its heart was proud of its height. How does pride bring a fall?
The trees of Eden were comforted at the cedar's fall. What does this teach about the end of the proud?
Pharaoh is compared to a sea monster brought low. What does this show about God's power over the mighty?
The mighty nations lie together in the pit. What does this show about the end of all human power apart from God?
God made Ezekiel a watchman. Who has God given you to care for?
"As I live, declares the Lord God, I have no pleasure in the death of the wicked, but that the wicked turn from his way and live." What does this show about God?
The people listened to Ezekiel like a love song but did not obey. How do you respond to God's word?
God condemns shepherds who fed themselves and not the sheep. What does good shepherding look like?
"I myself will search for my sheep and will seek them out... I will seek the lost, and I will bring back the strayed." How does Jesus fulfil this?
God will set over them one shepherd, his servant David. How does this point to Jesus?
"You are my sheep, human sheep of my pasture, and I am your God." What does it mean to be God's sheep?
Edom kept an ancient hatred. What grudges do you need to release?
Edom wanted to seize what belonged to God's people, but the Lord was there. What does it mean that God was there?
God acts for the sake of his holy name. Why does God's name matter?
"I will sprinkle clean water on you... A new heart I will give you, and a new spirit I will put within you." What does this new heart mean to you?
"This land that was desolate has become like the garden of Eden." Where do you long to see God restore?
God asked, "Can these bones live?" What feels dead that you need God to bring to life?
Breath came into the bones and they stood up. How does God's Spirit bring life?
"I will put my Spirit within you, and you shall live." What does this promise mean for you?
God will make an everlasting covenant of peace and dwell among them. What does God's dwelling with us mean?
Gog gathers against God's people. What does this show about opposition to God?
"So I will show my greatness and my holiness and make myself known." How does God make himself known?
"My holy name I will make known in the midst of my people Israel." How does God make his name known through you?
"I will not hide my face anymore from them, when I pour out my Spirit." What does God's Spirit bring?
Ezekiel was shown a vision of a new temple and told to pay attention. What does it mean to look closely at what God shows you?
Every gate and court is measured carefully. What does this show about God preparing a place for his people?
The temple is measured in great detail. What does this show about God's care in building his dwelling?
The table "before the Lord" stood in the holy place. What does it mean to live your life before the Lord?
The priests had holy rooms where they kept the holy things. What does it mean to set apart what is holy?
The wall separated the holy from the common. How do you keep what is holy in your life?
The glory of the Lord returned to the temple. What does God's return to his people mean?
"This is the place of my throne... where I will dwell in the midst of the people forever." What does God's presence with us forever mean?
Ezekiel was to show the temple so the people would be ashamed of their sins. How does seeing God's holiness lead to repentance?
Ezekiel saw the glory of the Lord fill the temple and fell on his face. How do you respond to God's glory?
The faithful priests would come near to minister. What does faithfulness lead to?
Priests teach people the difference between holy and common. Who helps you understand what honours God?
A holy portion of land was set apart for the Lord. What part of your life is set apart for God?
"Put away violence and oppression, and execute justice and righteousness." How can you act with justice?
The prince and people worship together on the Sabbath. What does worshipping together mean to you?
The people entered by one gate and left by another. What might it mean to leave worship changed?
The water from the temple grew deeper and deeper. How has God's life grown deeper in you?
"Everything will live where the river goes." Where do you long for God's life to flow?
The trees bear fruit every month and their leaves are for healing. How does Revelation echo this picture?
Every tribe receives its portion. What does this show about God remembering each of his people?
The name of the city will be "The Lord Is There." What does it mean for God to be there with you?
